lead: Olympia's winters are long and wet, and its downtown sits on low fill at the edge of Puget Sound. Steady rain, king tides and crawl space moisture drive most water damage here.
risk: winter rain leaks, tidal flooding and crawl space moisture
risk_short: winter rain, tidal flooding, crawl spaces
why: Olympia gets most of its rain from fall through spring, often in long, steady storms. Moss grows fast on roofs here, holding water against shingles and clogging gutters. Leaks start slowly and may not show up until a ceiling stains or a wall gets soft. Many homes sit over crawl spaces that stay damp all winter. A small plumbing leak under the floor can rot joists and grow mold before anyone notices.

Much of downtown Olympia was built on fill placed over tide flats in the late 1800s and early 1900s. When very high king tides meet low air pressure and heavy rain, water from Budd Inlet can push into downtown streets and storm drains. The city plans for rising seas. About 12% of Olympia homes were built before 1940, mostly in older neighborhoods near downtown.

tips: Clean moss off the roof and clear gutters each fall.
Add a vapor barrier and keep crawl space vents working.
Watch king tide forecasts if you live or work downtown.
Have tall trees near the house checked by an arborist.
areas: Calls come from Downtown, Eastside, Westside, South Capitol, Bigelow, Wildwood and Northeast, plus Lacey, Tumwater and Yelm.

faq.q: Why does my Olympia crawl space stay wet?
faq.a: Western Washington's long, wet winters keep soil damp, and poor drainage or a missing vapor barrier lets that moisture into the crawl space. A slow plumbing leak can add more. DryFlare can dry the wood and treat mold, and a vapor barrier and good drainage help keep it dry.
